claims.text: Enhanced local chemical short-range order in equiatomic FCC multi-component alloys increases spatial fluctuations in shear-fault energy.
Spatial fluctuations in shear-fault energy produce localized hard atomic motifs.
Hard atomic motifs act as pinning sites that impede dislocation glide.
Resistance caused by local shear-fault-energy fluctuations is a major source of strength in complex concentrated alloys.
Enhanced short-range order modifies strain-hardening behavior.
Equiatomic CrCoNi or NiCoCr can be prepared as an FCC random solid solution initial state.
Prolonged moderate-temperature annealing promotes enhanced local short-range order.
Minor additions of Mn or Fe promote enhanced local short-range order in the proposed equiatomic FCC alloy.
Rapid quenching retains a predominantly random chemical arrangement with minimal local ordering.
Regions of elevated local shear-fault energy increase barriers to dislocation motion.
Successive pinning at high-local-fault-energy sites produces non-uniform, wavy or jumpy dislocation paths.
Samples with enhanced short-range order will have a statistically significant increase in yield strength relative to a random baseline.
Enhanced-short-range-order samples will exhibit distinctly more wavy or pinned dislocation configurations than the random baseline.
Changes in shear-fault energy can alter the activation or propagation of partial dislocations and other FCC deformation mechanisms.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply to equiatomic FCC high-entropy alloys under moderate annealing and room-temperature testing.
Applicability to non-FCC systems or extreme temperatures is uncertain.
The magnitude of strengthening and the quantitative relationship between short-range order and mechanical properties remain uncertain.
A lack of yield-strength increase, altered strain hardening, and distinct dislocation structures in the enhanced-order samples would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The comparison is presented as isolating short-range order, but the optional Mn or Fe addition changes alloy composition and may destroy the stated equiatomic ternary comparison. Thus composition, rather than only ordering, would differ from the baseline.
